entities.summary: Hartwig of Uthlede was a German nobleman who played a crucial role in the Livonian Crusade. As Hartwig II, he served as Prince-Archbishop of Bremen from 1189 until his death in 1207. Born around 1150, Hartwig was a key figure in the Second Crusade, leading a military campaign against the pagan Livonian tribes in present-day Latvia and Estonia. His efforts helped establish the Bishopric of Ösel-Wiek, which remained a crucial outpost for the Teutonic Knights. Hartwig's legacy extends beyond his military achievements, as he also oversaw the construction of several churches and monasteries throughout his territories. His impact on the region was significant, paving the way for the spread of Christianity and the establishment of the Hanseatic League. Despite his passing, Hartwig's name remains etched in the annals of history, a testament to his enduring legacy as a leader and a statesman. The fact that he died in 1207, a year that would mark the beginning of the Albigensian Crusade, underscores the complexities of medieval politics and the ongoing struggles between Christianity and paganism.
